articles.title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
articles.authors: Borsheim S, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Gjertsen JE, Furnes O, Dybvik E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture by femoral component design and fixation method, stratified by sex and age
articles.take_home: Cemented composite beam femoral components had the lowest risk of fracture and should be preferred for men over 75 and women over 70. Polished taper-slip components had a high fracture risk in men of all ages and should generally be avoided.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life following periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty : a propensity score-matched cohort study with trajectory analysis.
articles.authors: Ablett AD, Powell-Bowns MFR, Super JT, Neo C, Yapp LZ, Clement ND, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients who had a periprosthetic femoral fracture after primary total hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 140 patients with fracture, matched with 700 general population controls
articles.outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-3L, EQ-VAS, and Oxford Hip Score at median 2.9 years after fracture
articles.take_home: About two-thirds of patients had a meaningful drop in quality of life after breaking the bone around their hip replacement, and one in ten felt their health was worse than death. The fracture erased about a third of the benefit patients had gained from their original hip replacement operation.

articles.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
articles.authors: Downie S, Kennedy M, Farhan-Alanie OM, Kennedy IW, McKean G, Kelly MP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study from prospectively collected database
articles.population: Patients with metastatic bone disease involving the hip undergoing femoral reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Reintervention for femoral implant failure (primary endpoint); complications requiring further surgery; overall survival. Two-year probability of reintervention 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025); five-year probability of reintervention 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025); overall complication rate 8% with three reinterventions for periprosthetic femoral fractures.
articles.take_home: A long uncemented hip implant used to treat metastatic cancer in the thighbone had very low rates of implant failure and revision surgery, with no cases of implant loosening in the medium term. This type of implant may be a good option for selected patients with metastatic bone disease around the hip.

articles.title: Long-term use of opioids and neuropathic medication after diaphyseal humerus fractures with or without nerve injury: a nationwide register-based cohort study of 4,185 patients.
articles.authors: Nyman E, Andersson S, Perez R, Zimmerman M, Merlo J, Dahlin LB
articles.population: Individuals with diaphyseal humerus fractures in Sweden, with and without nerve injury, treated operatively or non-operatively
articles.outcomes: High opioid use (≥60% of days covered per year) and neuropathic pain medication use in first and second years post-fracture
articles.take_home: Patients with humerus fractures used substantially more painkillers, especially opioids, in the first year after injury if they had surgery and nerve damage. Even in the second year, those treated without surgery but with nerve injury continued to use high levels of opioids. Women, older patients, and those with lower income or living alone were at particular risk of prolonged medication use.

articles.title: Segmental phase angle as predictor of activities of daily living and muscle health in patients with osteoporotic fracture A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Ito Y, Yoshimura Y, Nagano F, Matsumoto A
articles.population: Patients with osteoporotic fractures admitted to convalescent rehabilitation wards
articles.outcomes: Functional Independence Measure motor score, handgrip strength, and skeletal muscle mass index at discharge
articles.take_home: Leg phase angle (a measure of muscle quality) was associated with better everyday activities, muscle strength, and muscle mass in older patients recovering from osteoporotic fractures. Phase angle measurements may help identify which patients need targeted interventions during rehabilitation.

articles.title: Union rate and time to union following platelet-rich plasma therapy in fracture nonunion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Regmi A, Saini R, Baral S, Jain VK, Kulshrestha S, Iyengar KP
articles.population: Patients with fracture nonunion
articles.outcomes: Union rate and time to union
articles.take_home: Platelet-rich plasma may help more fractures heal successfully compared to standard treatment, but studies were small and used different methods, so we cannot yet be certain it works better or speeds up healing.

articles.title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association.
articles.authors: Latifi R, Kornvig S, Mohaddes M, Ali M, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for primary osteoarthritis or childhood hip disorder sequelae
articles.outcomes: All-cause cup revision rates comparing cemented and uncemented acetabular cups, stratified by age and sex, over follow-up periods of 0-1 years, 1-6 years, and 6-26 years
articles.take_home: Cemented cups had a lower risk of revision in the first year after hip replacement in older patients, but a higher revision risk after 6 years. In patients aged 80 years or older, there was no clear difference between cemented and uncemented cups after the first year.

articles.title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.
articles.authors: Takaiso H, Nomura K, Watanabe T, Nitta Y, Heak A, Im S, et al.
articles.population: Public referral hospitals and healthcare providers in Battambang Province, Cambodia
articles.sample_size: Seven public referral hospitals; physicians and 38 nurse pairs assessed
articles.outcomes: Emergency equipment availability, physician clinical skills in stroke and trauma scenarios, nurse basic life support skills
articles.take_home: Emergency care capacity in rural Cambodia is severely limited, especially at basic care hospitals which lack essential equipment like intubation devices and crash carts, and staff struggle with key clinical skills such as airway management and correct chest compression technique. The study recommends prioritising low-cost training and basic emergency care improvements at lower-level facilities.

articles.title: A scoping review evaluating artificial intelligence applications across various injury prevention domains.
articles.authors: Othman Y, Kasabwala D, Jayagopi K, Lemoine J, Park D, Hamza D, et al.
articles.study_type: Scoping review of artificial intelligence applications for injury prevention
articles.population: Studies evaluating AI for prevention of self-harm, suicide, abuse, violence, falls, and sports injuries
articles.outcomes: Predictive accuracy of machine learning models (measured by AUC scores) across different injury prevention domains; identification of modifiable risk factors
articles.take_home: Machine learning models show promise for predicting injuries and harm across multiple areas including self-harm, suicide, violence, falls and sports injuries, often outperforming traditional screening methods. However, the evidence is still limited and more research is needed before these tools can be routinely used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Early fecal diversion versus no initial diversion in blunt open pelvic fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of pelvic infection and mortality.
articles.authors: Ferrari F, Ancieta MDH, Laura LYS, Botti M
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
articles.population: Patients with blunt open pelvic fractures
articles.sample_size: 18 observational comparative reports; 171 participants for infection analysis, 236 for mortality analysis
articles.outcomes: Pelvic infection and short-term mortality in early fecal diversion versus no initial diversion
articles.take_home: The evidence does not clearly show that early fecal diversion reduces pelvic infection or mortality in blunt open pelvic fractures. The available studies were of low quality and had significant limitations, so we cannot yet say whether this treatment definitely helps or harms certain patients.

articles.title: New developments in locking plate osteosynthesis - A narrative review.
articles.authors: Braun BJ, Rosslenbroich S, Menger MM, Histing T
articles.outcomes: Evolution of plate osteosynthesis design including anatomical innovations, mechanobiologically optimised plates and systems for monitoring fracture healing
articles.take_home: This review describes how bone plates have improved over recent decades, moving from simple designs to anatomically shaped plates that can be inserted with smaller cuts and some newer plates can monitor how well the bone is healing.

articles.title: The use of PMMA bone cement in trauma surgery: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Holla M, Migdad H, Blokhuis T
articles.population: Trauma surgery patients
articles.outcomes: Material properties, biological behaviour, and clinical applications of PMMA bone cement in trauma surgery including prosthesis fixation, screw augmentation, temporary and permanent spacer use
articles.take_home: PMMA bone cement is a versatile and inexpensive tool in trauma surgery that can strengthen implant fixation in weak bone, serve as a temporary spacer during staged reconstruction, and in selected cases function as a permanent implant when combined with stable internal fixation.

articles.title: Surface topography and nanostructural modifications for the prevention of bacterial infections.
articles.authors: Graziani G, Ghezzi D
articles.population: Orthopaedic and trauma implants at risk of bacterial infection
articles.outcomes: Comparison of surface patterning versus nanostructured metallic coatings for preventing bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation on implants
articles.take_home: Nanostructured metallic coatings show more promise than surface patterning alone for preventing implant infections, though neither approach is yet available in clinical practice. Coatings that release ions or kill bacteria on contact appear more effective in real-world conditions than textured surfaces designed to physically deter bacteria.

articles.title: Cerclage wiring: Innovations and applications.
articles.authors: Forch S, Sandriesser S, Fenwick A, Augat P, Mayr E
articles.population: Patients with tibial fractures and humeral shaft fractures, including geriatric and younger patients
articles.outcomes: Stiffness of osteosynthesis constructs, weight-bearing capability, complication rates, rehabilitation speed, patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Modern cerclage wiring (cable fixation) added to plates or nails can make fracture fixation stronger and may allow patients to put full weight on their leg immediately after surgery. Early studies suggest this approach is safe, helps patients recover faster and improves their satisfaction in the weeks after surgery.

articles.title: Overview and new developments in intramedullary and cephalomedullary nailing.
articles.authors: Hackl S, Weisemann F, Trapp O, von Ruden C
articles.population: Patients with fractures of long bones, including epiphyseal, diaphyseal and metaphyseal fractures, nonunions, and femoral fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture reduction quality, anatomical axis restoration, rotational alignment, implant stability, bone healing rates, early functional rehabilitation and weight bearing
articles.take_home: Intramedullary nailing is an effective technique for treating long bone fractures as it provides strong stability and allows patients to move and bear weight early, which helps bones heal well. The quality of fracture reduction and correct screw positioning are the most important factors for successful outcomes.

articles.title: Review of a "Bone Glue Fixation" development.
articles.authors: Procter P
articles.population: Not specified
articles.outcomes: Development of a bone adhesive formulation based on phosphoserine, calcium salts and water that meets clinical requirements for bone glue
articles.take_home: Researchers have developed a new bone glue called Osstic that combines an amino acid called phosphoserine with calcium salts and water, and it has now been used in patients for the first time after showing promising results in laboratory tests.

articles.title: Alternate non-metallic implants in fracture care - A review.
articles.authors: Fritz T, Osche D, Liodakis E, Orth M
articles.population: Fracture patients, with emphasis on ageing population with fragility and pathological fractures
articles.outcomes: Biomechanical properties, clinical applications, outcomes and complications of CFR-PEEK implants and photodynamic bone stabilization implants
articles.take_home: Non-metallic implants such as CFR-PEEK and photodynamic bone stabilization are emerging alternatives to traditional metal implants that may better match bone's mechanical properties and reduce stress shielding. These approaches could be particularly helpful for older patients with weak bones, though they remain niche products in fracture treatment.

articles.title: Innovation in external fixation: Emerging hardware, software and automation technologies.
articles.authors: Raj S, Fornasiero M, Tsang SJ
articles.outcomes: Hardware design improvements, software for deformity analysis and planning, remote patient support systems, automated strut technologies
articles.take_home: External fixation technology has advanced significantly over the past 20 years with improvements in frame design, computer planning tools and automated systems to reduce the burden on patients. However, robust clinical evidence for many newer technologies remains limited.

articles.title: Modernizing preoperative planning in orthopaedic trauma surgery.
articles.authors: Leland CR, Farid AR, Stenquist DS, Suneja N, von Keudell AG
articles.outcomes: Application of 3D reconstruction, automated segmentation, and finite element analysis to preoperative planning in orthopaedic trauma surgery; assessment of how plate positioning and screw configuration affect construct stability
articles.take_home: Current preoperative planning in trauma surgery relies mainly on surgeon experience, but new computer-based methods using 3D imaging and biomechanical modelling can help surgeons optimise their choice of fixation devices before operating. These tools may eventually be integrated with surgical navigation and robotic systems to improve outcomes.

articles.title: Patient-specific instrument with 3D printing technology in orthopaedic trauma: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Wong PY, Liu C, Tao H, Li B, Yang M, Zhao C, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients undergoing fracture surgery
articles.outcomes: Operative time, surgical accuracy of wire and screw placement, functional outcomes
articles.take_home: 3D-printed surgical guides improved accuracy of wire and screw placement and reduced operation time compared with conventional surgery, though functional results were similar. Patient-specific metal implants made with 3D printing show promise but need further research.

articles.title: Generation Z and engagement in orthopaedic trauma: A multigenerational qualitative study.
articles.authors: Blokhuis TJ, Holla M, Gomez Vallejo J, Maqungo S, Dunbar RP
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma residents and senior consultants from Europe, North America, South America, Africa, and Asia
articles.outcomes: Perspectives on professional identity, work intensity, academic engagement, and work-life integration in orthopaedic trauma
articles.take_home: Younger orthopaedic surgeons in training are committed to trauma surgery but prioritise work-life boundaries and paid recognition for academic work differently from senior surgeons, who view unpaid academic engagement as part of their professional duty. Understanding these generational differences may help healthcare systems attract and retain younger surgeons in demanding specialties.

articles.title: Tight rope fixation in fracture management.
articles.authors: Keating JF
articles.population: Patients with ankle fractures with diastasis, lateral third clavicular fractures, acromioclavicular dislocations, and Lisfranc injuries
articles.outcomes: Malunion rates, implant-related complications, need for implant removal, functional outcomes
articles.take_home: Tightrope fixation using metal buttons and sutures appears to work well for ankle fractures and clavicle injuries, with some studies suggesting fewer complications and better outcomes than traditional screw fixation. However, more high-quality research is needed to fully understand where these implants work best.

articles.title: Adherent antimicrobial coatings for orthopaedic implants - A narrative review.
articles.authors: Montali A, D'Este M, Moriarty TF, Alt V
articles.population: Orthopaedic and trauma patients at risk of fracture-related infections
articles.outcomes: Safety and efficacy of antimicrobial coatings; cost effectiveness; infection prevention and management
articles.take_home: Antimicrobial coatings on orthopaedic implants show promise in preventing infections, with silver-coated joint replacements having the longest track record. Although these coatings are more expensive, they appear cost-effective in higher-risk patients as the cost of treating an infection is much greater than the cost of using a coated implant.

articles.title: Distal femur plate-nail constructs. Belt and suspenders?
articles.authors: Chana-Rodriguez F, Rojo-Manaute JM, Latif GS, Al Ismaily HM, Dunbar R
articles.population: Patients with distal femoral fractures and non-unions
articles.outcomes: Total complications, reoperations, operative duration, blood loss, hospital stay
articles.take_home: Combined nail-plate fixation for distal femur fractures may reduce complications and need for further surgery compared to single fixation methods, without taking longer or causing more bleeding. However, evidence is currently limited to retrospective studies and stronger research is needed.

articles.title: Past, present and future of distal radius corrective osteotomy: From 2D based reconstruction to 3D data-driven, patient specific care.
articles.authors: Loonen TGJ, Maal TJJ, Edwards MJR, Stirler VMA
articles.population: Patients with distal radius malunion requiring corrective osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of deformity correction, functional outcomes, cost-effectiveness of treatment
articles.take_home: Distal radius osteotomy planning has progressed from simple 2D X-ray based methods to advanced 3D virtual planning using CT scans and patient-specific guides, though better surgical precision does not yet guarantee better functional results. Future improvements require standardised evaluation methods and larger studies to determine whether these advanced techniques truly deliver better, cost-effective care for patients.

articles.title: 3D printed scaffolds for reconstruction of segmental long bone defects: A mini narrative review.
articles.authors: Gilissen MJV, Lodewijks AJL, Vissers-Van der Broeck LCA, Blokhuis TJ, van Griensven M, Poeze M
articles.population: Patients with large segmental long bone defects
articles.outcomes: Mechanical stability, bone regeneration, osteointegration, degradation profiles, and long-term clinical outcomes of 3D-printed scaffolds
articles.take_home: 3D-printed scaffolds made from metal, ceramic, polymer or composite materials show promise for reconstructing large bone defects, but current evidence is limited by small patient numbers and lack of long-term follow-up data. More standardised designs and clinical trials are needed to determine which scaffold type works best.

articles.title: Mini-fragment applications for lower extremity long bone fractures: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Dunbar RP, Sorkin AT, Alismaily HM, Chana-Rodriguez F
articles.population: Lower extremity long bone fractures
articles.outcomes: Applications and rationale for mini-fragment fixation systems (2.0, 2.4 and 2.7 mm) in lower extremity fracture surgery
articles.take_home: Mini-fragment implants, originally used only for hand and foot fractures, are now useful tools for surgeons treating complex lower leg fractures. They can be used alongside larger fixation devices, on their own in certain cases, or to temporarily stabilise fractures.

articles.title: Stable 2-year migration on radiostereometric analysis and improved gait speed and function after bicruciate-retaining TKA: a prospective cohort of 25 patients.
articles.authors: Mills K, Van Laarhoven SN, Defoort KC, Susan S, Heesterbeek PJC
articles.population: Patients undergoing bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Component migration measured by radiostereometric analysis at 2 years; gait speed, stride length and stride time; patient-reported outcome measures; adverse events
articles.take_home: The knee replacement components showed stable fixation at 2 years with very small amounts of movement. Patients reported significant improvements in quality of life after surgery, though their walking speed improved slightly less than the meaningful clinical threshold.

articles.title: Arthroplasty versus internal fixation for displaced femoral neck fractures in older patients with dementia: a target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Jensen SS, Gundtoft PH, Nelissen RGHH, Gjertsen JE, Pedersen AB
articles.study_type: Observational comparative-effectiveness study using target trial emulation framework
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and over with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: Primary: reoperation within 365 days. Secondary: major reoperation, mortality, length of stay, early mobilisation, and mobility decline
articles.take_home: Internal fixation was associated with fewer repeat operations and lower mortality than arthroplasty in older patients with dementia and a broken hip, though the researchers note that confounding factors and differences in how outcomes were recorded may have affected these findings.

articles.title: Enhanced wound healing potential of a carboxymethyl cellulose/gelatin-based hydrogel containing decellularized amniotic membrane and Matricaria chamomilla extract: A multifunctional composite dressing.
articles.authors: Zamani S, Ghorbani M, Molzemi S, Farahani MK, Raei M
articles.population: Full-thickness wound model (in vivo)
articles.outcomes: Wound closure rate at day 14, fibroblast viability, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, antibacterial activity, tissue regeneration including re-epithelialization and collagen deposition
articles.take_home: A new composite dressing made from carboxymethyl cellulose, gelatin, chamomile extract and processed amniotic membrane closed wounds faster in animals (86% closure at day 14) compared to a dressing without chamomile (79%) or a commercial dressing (59%). The dressing also showed antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties that may help wounds heal better.

articles.title: Can posterolateral tibial plateau fractures be treated with an anterolateral approach? A biomechanical study on novel plating concepts in artificial tibia models.
articles.authors: Zderic I, Llano L, Menze J, Altmann M, Breceda A, Herbst E, et al.
articles.study_type: Biomechanical laboratory study using artificial bone models
articles.population: Artificial tibia models simulating posterolateral tibial plateau fractures
articles.outcomes: Fragment displacement, posterior tilt, cycles to clinical failure, and loads at clinical failure under progressively increasing cyclic loading
articles.take_home: A lateral plate with a posterior extension or with extra screws can stabilise posterolateral tibial plateau fractures as well as the standard posterolateral plate approach, suggesting the easier-to-access front approach might work clinically. However, a lateral plate alone without reinforcement performed poorly and needs further testing in actual patients.

articles.title: Where is trauma care delivered in New York state? A statewide analysis of distribution and outcomes by trauma center level.
articles.authors: Patel P, Mon NO, Angus LDG, Szydziak E, Cardozo-Stolberg S, Swezey E, et al.
articles.population: Trauma inpatients aged 15 years and older in New York State
articles.outcomes: Mortality, complications, discharge dispositions, and hospital length of stay
articles.take_home: Trauma outcomes vary significantly between hospital types depending on injury severity, with higher-level trauma centres treating more severe cases. The findings suggest there are opportunities to improve how patients are directed to appropriate hospitals and how trauma services allocate resources.

articles.title: Variations in hip fracture management at trauma vs. non-trauma centers.
articles.authors: Harris B, Benson E
articles.population: Adults with hip fractures (excluding polytrauma patients)
articles.sample_size: 135 patients (104 at trauma hospital, 31 at non-trauma hospital)
articles.outcomes: Hospital length of stay, time from admission to surgery, operative duration
articles.take_home: The non-trauma hospital treated hip fracture patients faster and discharged them sooner than the trauma hospital, even though it had sicker patients. This suggests non-trauma hospitals may be better equipped than trauma hospitals for managing hip fractures in this healthcare system.

articles.title: Comprehensive treatment approaches for traumatic tattoos: An integrative review.
articles.authors: Haik J, Levi Y, Kornhaber R, Cleary M, Beylin D, Tasigiorgos S, et al.
articles.population: People with traumatic tattoos (pigment driven into skin by injury)
articles.sample_size: 27 studies reviewed, mostly case reports and small series
articles.outcomes: Effectiveness of laser therapy, mechanical debridement and other treatments for removing traumatic tattoos
articles.take_home: Combining quick removal of foreign material within 24 hours of injury with laser treatment appears to work best, though the evidence is limited and better quality studies are needed. Q-switched lasers generally achieved good to excellent clearance with mostly temporary side effects.

articles.title: Patterns of depression screening, referral, and behavioral health follow-up after orthopaedic trauma.
articles.authors: Reddy S, Cahill M, Schimizzi G, Fram B, Erdman MK, Christiano A
articles.population: Adult orthopaedic trauma patients at a Level I trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Proportion screening positive for depression (PHQ-9 >10), rates of moderately severe to severe depression (PHQ-9 ≥15), behavioural health referral completion rates, and six-month orthopaedic complications
articles.take_home: Nearly 45% of orthopaedic trauma patients screened positive for depression, but only 34% of those referred for behavioural health support actually attended appointments, compared to 68% in non-trauma orthopaedic patients. Patients who did not complete their behavioural health referral had significantly higher rates of wound infections and unplanned hospital visits.

articles.title: Predictors of 30-day mortality and complications following surgical treatment of pathologic hip fractures.
articles.authors: Thomas G, Njoku-Austin CO, Almeida ND, Sinha S, Schrand TV, Mirvish A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over undergoing hip fracture surgery, comparing those with pathologic fractures to non-pathologic fractures
articles.sample_size: 204,675 hip fracture patients, of which 6,159 (2.9%) had pathologic fractures
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality, postoperative complications (cardiac, transfusion, renal, venous thromboembolic, infectious and neurological complications)
articles.take_home: Patients with pathologic hip fractures had higher death rates and complication rates than those with non-pathologic fractures. Factors that reduced death risk included not having advanced cancer, being functionally independent before surgery, and not having a history of sepsis, whilst low platelet counts and anaemia increased death and complication risk.

articles.title: Video-assisted resident education is associated with improved ankle joint reduction: A prospective controlled study.
articles.authors: Bilodeau RE, Hall AJ, Como M, Cautela F, Rowe J, Joseph D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with ankle fractures (OTA/AO type 44) requiring bivalved short leg cast or AO splint at a level I trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 280 consecutive ankle fractures: 111 in intervention group, 169 in control group
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: radiographic joint reduction quality (tibiofibular overlap, tibiofibular clear space, medial clear space). Secondary outcomes: splint padding thickness and ankle dorsiflexion angle.
articles.take_home: Residents who received video-assisted education achieved better ankle joint reduction quality, particularly for the most severe fracture types. More ankles were also splinted in the correct position with the video training, though overall splint padding thickness did not improve significantly.

articles.title: Ischemic severity rather than ischemic time is associated with major limb complications in traumatic popliteal artery injury: A retrospective case series.
articles.authors: Izawa Y, Futamura K, Nishida M
articles.population: Patients with blunt traumatic popliteal artery injury
articles.outcomes: Extensive soft tissue defects requiring reconstruction and amputation
articles.take_home: How severe the lack of blood flow is when the patient arrives, rather than how long they wait for surgery, is what matters most for whether the leg will have serious problems. Limbs with the worst blood flow (grade III) or no backup blood vessels were much more likely to develop major complications, even if surgery happened quickly.

articles.title: Opportunistic assessment of bone quality using CT-derived hounsfield units in postmenopausal women with femoral trochanteric fractures.
articles.authors: Terada C, Yokoo S
articles.population: Postmenopausal women aged 65 years or older with femoral trochanteric fractures treated with intramedullary nailing
articles.outcomes: CT-derived Hounsfield unit measurements compared with DXA T-scores to identify markedly low bone mineral density
articles.take_home: CT scans taken at admission can help identify patients with very weak bones, though the method is not fully reliable yet. The researchers found a moderate link between CT measurements and bone density scores, but the test needs further validation before it can be widely used to guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Thoracic irrigation in managing traumatic hemothorax: A concise review of techniques and practice variations.
articles.authors: Indorewala Y, Prashar S, Nishida C, Nasef Y, Othman Y, Haddadi M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with traumatic hemothorax treated with tube thoracostomy
articles.sample_size: Six studies included in the review
articles.outcomes: Need for secondary intervention, hospital length of stay, hospital-free days, retained haemothorax
articles.take_home: Adding thoracic irrigation to standard chest tube drainage for traumatic bleeding in the lung cavity reduces the need for further treatment and shortens hospital stays. The optimal amount of fluid to use and the best tube size remain unclear.

articles.title: Do radiographic surrogates of pre-bend appropriateness influence outcomes after titanium elastic nailing in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures?
articles.authors: Saritas TB, Yucel MH, Parlak S, Arici V, Tan A, Yalcinkaya A, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 5-11 years with femoral mid-shaft fractures treated with titanium elastic nailing
articles.outcomes: Radiographic coronal angulation, limb length discrepancy, and complications
articles.take_home: Proper pre-bending of titanium elastic nails (meeting technical criteria) was linked to less coronal angulation on X-rays, but whether this difference matters clinically remains unclear. The study could not definitively determine if meeting these criteria reduces actual complications.

articles.title: Scapular fracture and risk of great vessel injury in geriatric blunt trauma: A TQIP analysis.
articles.authors: Peisepar M, Rafieezadeh A, Prabhakaran K, Nair H, Kannichamy V, Harikrishnan S, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and over with blunt trauma injury
articles.outcomes: Great vessel injury, in-hospital mortality, length of stay
articles.take_home: In older adults, a scapular fracture alone does not increase the risk of major blood vessel injury, but when combined with a sternal fracture, the risk is significantly higher and warrants further imaging to check for subclavian artery injury.

articles.title: Orthopedic trauma in patients with opioid use disorder: Current concepts in perioperative management.
articles.authors: Stout JW, Keenan J, Rehman S
articles.study_type: Current concepts review of peer-reviewed literature
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients with opioid use disorder
articles.outcomes: Infection rates, nonunion, revision surgery, prolonged hospitalisation, and readmission; perioperative management approaches including medication-assisted treatment, multimodal analgesia, and regional anaesthesia
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic trauma patients with opioid use disorder have higher rates of complications like infection and nonunion, but evidence supports continuing their addiction treatment during surgery and using multiple pain relief methods rather than avoiding or only using opioids. Early involvement of addiction and pain specialists, along with coordinated discharge planning, gives the best outcomes.

articles.title: The downside of the pull-up: A 10-year national analysis of emergency department visits, 2015-2024.
articles.authors: Shabbir R, Layton B, Kang Z, Kim B, Rehman S, Galos DK
articles.study_type: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of national emergency department data
articles.population: Patients presenting to emergency departments with pull-up bar injuries
articles.outcomes: Injury patterns by age, body region, diagnosis, location, and mechanism; most injuries were head, face, or upper-extremity trauma with laceration, head injury, or fracture as leading diagnoses
articles.take_home: Pull-up bar injuries send roughly 4000 people to emergency departments each year in the US, mostly young people and children, with head and face injuries being most common. The good news is that over 93 percent of these injuries are treated and released without needing surgery.

articles.title: How the cause of surgical delay affects mortality in fragility hip fractures: A cohort study.
articles.authors: Senan R, Karthik P, Dhilon P, Howard T, Rayan F, Kirmani S, et al.
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged over 60
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality and 1-year mortality
articles.take_home: Delays caused by lack of operating theatre space did not increase death rates, but delays caused by the need to stabilise patients' medical conditions were associated with higher mortality. Getting patients who are medically fit to theatre quickly matters, but the main focus should be on preparing patients properly before surgery rather than simply rushing them through.

articles.title: The blunt truth: The role of marijuana in PTSD after intentional traumatic injury.
articles.authors: Kern JA, Wilson C, Joshi SA, Ghio M, O'Neill K, Reese J, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients admitted to a level-1 trauma centre who had experienced intentional traumatic injury (interpersonal violence)
articles.outcomes: Association between PTSD and marijuana use at follow-up; quality of life scores on PROMIS-29
articles.take_home: Survivors of interpersonal violence who developed PTSD were seven times more likely to use marijuana at follow-up, and also reported higher marijuana use before the injury. Screening for marijuana use alongside psychological assessment might help identify patients at risk of developing PTSD after trauma.

articles.title: Basic science and surgical timing for polytrauma patients.
articles.authors: Pedrick E, Pfeifer R, Schemitsch E, Teuben M, Vallier H, Haller J, et al.
articles.population: Polytrauma patients
articles.outcomes: Emerging diagnostic tools (lipidomics as biomarkers) and treatment timing algorithms for fracture fixation in polytrauma
articles.take_home: Current blood tests struggle to predict which polytrauma patients can safely have early fracture surgery. New blood tests called lipidomics may help doctors decide which patients need surgery within 24 hours and which need a more cautious approach, especially those with serious head injuries.

articles.title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
articles.authors: Le V, Watson JT, McBride-Gagyi S, Priddy LB, Glatt V, Hixon KR, et al.
articles.population: Patients with orthopaedic trauma requiring bone and soft tissue repair
articles.outcomes: Regenerative biomaterials including improved Masquelet induced membranes, hydroxyapatite-coated magnesium scaffolds, Biomimetic Hematoma scaffolds, and application of 3R principles framework
articles.take_home: Four experts presented emerging regenerative biomaterials and engineering approaches that aim to improve bone and soft tissue repair after orthopaedic trauma. These developments focus on making treatments biologically informed and clinically effective whilst being ethically responsible.

articles.title: Emerging concepts in the diagnosis and treatment of fracture-related infections.
articles.authors: Pedrick E, Certain L, Yoon R, Natoli RM, Gitajn IL, Tang Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients with fracture-related infections
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy and treatment effectiveness for fracture-related infections
articles.take_home: New tools like molecular testing and special imaging techniques may help doctors diagnose bone infections more accurately and remove infected tissue more effectively. Studies show that oral antibiotics work as well as intravenous antibiotics for treating these infections, whilst avoiding the risks of long-term IV treatment.

articles.title: AI: It's in your phone, why not in your practice?
articles.authors: Yang L, Marmor M, Mell S, Lockhart T, Anderson DD
articles.study_type: Review article and position statement from OTA AI Task Force
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma surgeons and patients
articles.outcomes: Identification of AI applications in orthopaedic trauma including fall risk prediction in elderly patients, automated image-based diagnosis and outcome assessment, and virtual patient cohorts for clinical trials
articles.take_home: Artificial intelligence is being developed for orthopaedic trauma care and is moving from research laboratories towards clinical use. For these tools to work best, data scientists and orthopaedic surgeons need to work together, with both academic and industry involvement.

articles.title: Quantitative decision-support strategies to enhance emergency medical service accessibility in high-risk freeway tunnels.
articles.authors: Jung S, Qin X
articles.study_type: Observational study with machine learning analysis
articles.population: In-tunnel motor vehicle crashes on Korean freeways
articles.outcomes: Crash severity prediction; identification of factors affecting emergency medical service response times and crash outcomes
articles.take_home: Crashes more than 1 km from tunnel entrances with poor emergency medical service coverage were more likely to be severe. Tunnels with emergency cross passages, multiple lanes, emergency parking areas and well-spaced camera systems had better outcomes.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve blocks reduce opioid requirements in the first 24 h following surgical fixation of acute tibial shaft fractures.
articles.authors: Khan UA, Quigley C, Schulman M, Holland J, Ghidei S, Kim A, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18-79 years with acute tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail fixation
articles.sample_size: 246 patients (78 received peripheral nerve blocks, 168 did not)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative opioid use in the first 24 hours (measured in morphine milligram equivalents), length of hospital stay, and incidence of acute compartment syndrome
articles.take_home: Peripheral nerve blocks reduced opioid requirements by 36% in the first 24 hours after tibial shaft fracture surgery, with average pain relief medication needs dropping from 138 to 73 units. However, careful monitoring for acute compartment syndrome remains essential when using nerve blocks, as delayed presentation may occur.

articles.title: Single crash, multiple stories: A finite mixture perspective of motorcycle injury severity with a focus on post-crash medical, rescue, human and roadway-environmental factors.
articles.authors: Zia-Ur-Rehman, Ahmad N, Ahmed A, Dong Z, Kiyani WI
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis using finite mixture Tobit regression modelling
articles.population: Motorcycle crash victims in Karachi, Pakistan
articles.outcomes: Injury Severity Score (ISS) in relation to Glasgow Coma Score, blood pressure, pre-hospital response time, evacuation mode, human factors (speeding, nighttime, wrong-way riding), and multi-vehicle involvement
articles.take_home: Severe brain injury and very low blood pressure significantly increased injury severity scores in motorcycle crashes, as did longer delays before hospital treatment. The study found that crash victims fell into two distinct groups with different injury patterns, suggesting that one-size-fits-all predictions of injury severity may not work for all motorcycle crash victims.

articles.title: Peripheral vascular trauma in a civilian Asian trauma centre: Epidemiology, management and outcomes over 9 years.
articles.authors: Chong FJ, Lee KRY, Go K, Tee MZQ, Chan YM, Hong Q, et al.
articles.population: Patients with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries from trauma
articles.sample_size: 180 patients with peripheral vascular injuries from 77,990 trauma admissions
articles.outcomes: Limb salvage rate, amputation rate, mortality, functional independence at discharge, complications
articles.take_home: Among patients with vascular injuries from trauma, 88% of lower limb injuries were successfully salvaged with surgery, with only 10% requiring amputation and 3% mortality. Most patients (93%) were functionally independent when discharged from hospital.
